The next cell sets the look of the plots below: the course colors, quiet grey labels and no frame. Run it once. A plot picks it up when you add `course_style...` to its keywords, after a semicolon.

```{julia}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
using Plots
# The course look for plots, used like this: bar(x, y; course_style...)
course_style = (
    palette=["#537E8F", "#F6B265", "#3D5369", "#A7C7C6", "#DB6B6B", "#FCCF9C"],
    background_color="#FFFDFC",
    fontfamily="Helvetica",
    titlefontfamily="Helvetica Bold",
    titlefontsize=18,
    titlefontcolor="#363D45",
    titlelocation=:left,
    foreground_color_text="#6B7480",
    foreground_color_guide="#6B7480",
    foreground_color_axis="#9AA1A8",
    foreground_color_border="#9AA1A8",
    yforeground_color_border="#FFFDFC", # no line on the left, the grid is enough
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=11,
    legendfontsize=11,
    foreground_color_legend=nothing,
    background_color_legend=nothing,
    grid=:y,
    gridcolor="#E8E4E0",
    gridalpha=1,
    framestyle=:axes,
    tick_direction=:none,
    yformatter=:plain,
    dpi=300,
    top_margin=4Plots.mm,
    left_margin=8Plots.mm,
    bottom_margin=6Plots.mm
)
```
